projectBackground.name: Parcelwise Order API
projectBackground.context: The orders endpoint takes 12 seconds to list orders and sometimes shows duplicates on page boundaries.

manager.name: Piotr Nowak
manager.note: Explain the cause, not just the patch. A fix without a reason will come back.

assignment.title: Diagnose and fix the orders API
assignment.brief: Count queries, calculate pagination, choose the right HTTP semantics, review a PR and write a clear bug summary.

documents.name: Slow Request Trace
documents.note: 200 orders listed; one query for orders, then one customer query per order.

documents.name: Pull Request #214
documents.note: Adds retry on payment creation without idempotency key.

tasks.title: N+1 Queries
tasks.prompt: The endpoint fetches 200 orders, then queries the customer for each order. How many queries run in total?
tasks.reasoning: One query for the list plus one per row is the N+1 pattern.
tasks.mistake: Missing N+1 leads to performance collapse as data grows.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Pagination
tasks.prompt: 1,037 records with page size 50. How many pages are needed?
tasks.mistake: Rounding down loses the final records.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Retries and Payments
tasks.prompt: The PR adds automatic retries to create a payment. What must be included?
options: An idempotency key so retries don't charge twice
tasks.reasoning: Retries on non-idempotent actions risk duplicates unless a key makes them safe.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Duplicates on Page Boundaries
tasks.prompt: Duplicates appear when new orders arrive between page requests using OFFSET. What is the better approach?
options: Cursor (keyset) pagination on a stable sort key
tasks.reasoning: Offset shifts as data changes; keyset anchors to a value.
tasks.tip: Sort by a unique stable key.
tasks.mistake: Offset pagination on changing data returns duplicates and gaps.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: PR Review Checklist
tasks.prompt: Select what a good reviewer checks.
options: Tests cover the behaviour and edge cases
tasks.reasoning: Review evaluates behaviour, safety and maintainability, not the author.
tasks.tip: Review the change, not the person.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Bug Summary
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence summary of the slow endpoint for the ticket.
tasks.modelAnswer: The orders endpoint ran 201 queries for 200 orders because customers were loaded one by one (N+1). This caused a 12 second response under load. I replaced it with a single joined query and added an index on orders.customer_id, which reduced the response to under 300 ms in staging. A regression test now fails if the query count exceeds three. I also switched pagination to a cursor to stop duplicates.
tasks.reasoning: A good summary has cause, fix, evidence and prevention.
tasks.mistake: A fix without a test often returns.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Double Charge
caseStudy.background: A payment service retried failed requests without an idempotency key. During a network blip 1,900 customers were charged twice; refunds and support cost €90,000.
caseStudy.challenges: Retries were added to improve reliability but made operations unsafe.
questions: Why are retries dangerous without idempotency?
How would you test for it?
caseStudy.solution: Forge required idempotency keys on every write endpoint and added a duplicate-request test.

options: One query plus one per row
